title: At the Pharmacy
subtitle: Asking for medicine and understanding how to take it
review: Written by Claude from Marissa's script: check the notes and the questions. No Burmese yet. The pharmacist (P) has no voice of her own: until one is chosen she is read by the course voice, which is also Emma's. Choose a second woman's voice before recording.
intro: Lucas has a cold and is sure it is the end, so Emma goes to the pharmacy for him: four short scenes. Listen for how she asks for medicine, the questions the pharmacist asks, and how to say how often and how long to take something.

lines.text: Emma… I think this is the end.
lines.note: He is joking: he feels so sick that he thinks he is dying.
A cold: a small illness with a runny nose and a sore throat.

lines.text: My throat hurts, my head hurts, everything hurts.
lines.note: My + part of the body + hurts. Everything hurts: all of me hurts.

lines.text: I'm going to the pharmacy. What do you need?
lines.note: A pharmacy sells medicine. Also a drugstore (American) or a chemist's (British).
A miracle: something wonderful that cannot really happen.

lines.text: I'll ask if they have one without a prescription.
lines.note: A prescription: a paper from a doctor. You need one for some medicines. One = a miracle.

lines.text: Hi, I'd like something for a cold, please.
lines.note: I'd like…, please: the polite way to ask in a shop. Something for + an illness: medicine for it.
Sure = yes, of course.
Symptoms: the signs of an illness, like a cough or a fever.

lines.text: He has a runny nose, he's coughing, and he complains a lot.
lines.note: A runny nose: water comes out of your nose. Complain: say again and again that something is bad.
A fever: your body is hotter than normal.
99 degrees Fahrenheit is 37.2 °C: only a little warm. Serious: very bad.
Allergic to…: something makes you sick, like nuts or cats.
Housework: cleaning, cooking, washing the dishes. He is not really allergic: he doesn't like doing it.

lines.text: OK. This cough syrup: one spoonful in the morning and one at night.
lines.note: Cough syrup: thick medicine you drink for a cough. A spoonful: one spoon of it.
Got it = I understand. Tablets: small pills you swallow.

lines.text: One tablet three times a day, with meals.
lines.note: Three times a day: morning, afternoon and evening. With meals: when you eat.

lines.text: Five days at most. If he doesn't feel better, he should see a doctor.
lines.note: At most: not more than. He should… gives advice.

lines.text: No, it's over the counter. That'll be nine forty.
lines.note: Over the counter: you can buy it without a prescription. That'll be… gives the price: $9.40.
By card: with a bank card. In cash: with money.
So? asks for the news. She: the pharmacist.

lines.text: One tablet three times a day, and syrup morning and night.
And how long do I have to stay in bed?
lines.note: Have to: must. Stay in bed: not get up.

lines.text: She said you can do the dishes tonight.
lines.note: She said (that) + a sentence tells you someone's words. Do the dishes: wash the plates and cups.
A question made by the voice going up, with no do or did.
She is joking. The box says how to take the medicine, not who does the dishes.

notes: Asking at the pharmacy: I'd like something for a cold / a cough / a headache, please.
Symptoms: a runny nose, a cough, a fever, a sore throat. He's coughing. My head hurts.
The pharmacist's questions: Is it for you? What are his symptoms? Does he have a fever? Is he allergic to anything?
How to take it: one tablet three times a day, with meals; one spoonful in the morning and one at night; five days at most.
A prescription: a paper from the doctor. Over the counter: no prescription needed.
Paying: That'll be nine forty. By card, please. In cash, please.
Fever in Fahrenheit: 98.6 °F is normal (37 °C). 99 °F is 37.2 °C.

questions.q: Emma wants medicine for Lucas. What does she say?
options: I'd like something for a cold, please.
I'd like a cold for my husband.
questions.why: I'd like something for + an illness: the polite way to ask for medicine.

options: A broken arm and a headache
A runny nose, a cough and a lot of complaining
A high fever and a stomachache
questions.why: He has a runny nose, he's coughing, and he complains a lot.

questions.q: How does Lucas take the tablets?
options: One in the morning and one at night
Three times a day, with meals
questions.why: The syrup is morning and night. The tablets: one tablet three times a day, with meals.

options: No, the medicine is over the counter.
questions.why: Over the counter: you can buy it without a prescription.

questions.q: What should Lucas do if he doesn't feel better after five days?
questions.why: If he doesn't feel better, he should see a doctor.

questions.q: Is Lucas really allergic to housework?
options: No. Emma means he doesn't like doing it.
questions.why: Emma is joking: Lucas doesn't like housework.
